copy.blurb:
Friday 26 June 2026 at 19:00 UTC. Norway and France on the card. On the France side, the engine's number sits +15.2pp clear of the market — one of the widest in the priced field this far out from kickoff.

Elo numbers going in: Norway 1760, France 2030. That's a 270-point lead for France — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Norway to win at 15%, the draw at 14%, and France to win at 71%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Norway to win at 20%, the draw at 24%, and France to win at 56%. The France side trades at 56% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of −127. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 71%, +15.2pp wider.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On France, that haircut lands the model at 64%; the market is at 56%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +7.8pp. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the France side specifically.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 35 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Bootstrap lower-bound on the France side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives France a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +15.2pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.

copy.summary: France are favourites on the market at 56% — and the model thinks the market is still underrating them. Our prior reads 71%, a +15.2pp upgrade that crosses the Pick threshold comfortably.
